paragraphs: The Bank of America Corporation (Bank of America; often abbreviated BAC, BofA, or, less commonly, BOA) is an American multinational bank and financial services holding company headquartered at the Bank of America Corporate Center in Charlotte, North Carolina, with investment banking and auxiliary headquarters in Manhattan. The bank was formed by the merger of NationsBank and the legacy corporation of Bank of America in 1998. It is the second-largest banking institution in the United States by consolidated assets, after JPMorgan Chase. It is also the second-largest bank in the world by market capitalization, after JPMorgan Chase.

Among the Big Four banking institutions and one of eight systemically important financial institutions in the United States; it competes with JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, and Wells Fargo. Its primary financial services revolve around commercial banking, wealth management, and investment banking.

Through past mergers, the oldest branch of the Bank of America franchise dates back to 1784, when Massachusetts Bank was chartered, becoming the first federally chartered joint-stock-owned bank in the United States. Another branch of its history goes back to the American-based Bank of Italy, founded by Amadeo Pietro Giannini in 1904, which provided various banking services to Italian immigrants who faced service discrimination at the time. Headquartered in San Francisco, California, Giannini helped develop and merged his interests  with Bank of America, Los Angeles in the 1920s and the combined bank eventually did business as Bank of America.

In the 1950s, the passage of landmark federal banking legislation facilitated rapid growth, quickly establishing prominent shares for the present bank's predecessors. After suffering significant losses during the 1998 Russian financial crisis, BankAmerica, as it was then known, was acquired by the Charlotte-based NationsBank for $62 billion. Following what was then the largest bank acquisition in history, the Bank of America Corporation was founded. Through a series of mergers and acquisitions, it built upon its commercial banking business by establishing Merrill Lynch for wealth management and Bank of America Merrill Lynch for investment banking in 2008 and 2009, respectively, and since renamed BofA Securities.

As of 2018, the investment bank was considered within the "bulge bracket" as the world's third-largest investment bank. Its wealth management unit then managing $1.08 trillion in assets under management (AUM) as the second-largest wealth manager in the world, after UBS. In commercial banking, Bank of America has operations, but does not maintain retail branches in all 50 states of the United States, Washington, D.C., and over 40 other countries.

The bank's large market share, business activities, and economic impact have led to numerous lawsuits and investigations regarding both mortgages and financial disclosures dating back to the 2008 financial crisis. Its corporate practices of servicing the middle class and wider banking community have yielded a substantial market share since the early 20th century. As of August 2018, Bank of America has a $313.5 billion market capitalization, making it the 13th largest company in the world.

people.title: Co-President

people.quote: James P. DeMare (56) Co-President since September 2025;

people.name: Hari Gopalkrishnan
people.title: Chief Technology and Information Officer

people.name: Geoffrey S. Greener
people.title: Chief Risk Officer
people.bio: Has served as Chief Risk Officer since April 2014. Previously served as Head of Enterprise Capital Management from April 2011 to April 2014.
people.quote: Geoffrey S. Greener (61) Chief Risk Officer since April 2014;

people.name: Bernard A. Mensah
people.title: President, International, CEO of Merrill Lynch International (MLI), BANA London Branch Head
people.bio: Has served as President, International, CEO of Merrill Lynch International and BANA London Branch Head since August 2020. Previously served as Co-Head of Global FICC Trading from March 2015 to September 2019.
people.quote: Bernard A. Mensah (57) President, International, CEO of Merrill Lynch International (MLI), BANA London Branch Head since August 2020.

people.name: Lauren A. Mogensen
people.title: Global General Counsel
people.bio: Has served as Global General Counsel since November 2021. Previously served as Head of Global Compliance & Operational Risk, and Reputational Risk from December 2013 to October 2021.
people.quote: Lauren A. Mogensen (63) Global General Counsel since November 2021;

people.name: Brian T. Moynihan
people.title: Chair of the Board and Chief Executive Officer
people.bio: Has served as Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Board of Directors since January 2010, and Chair of the Board since October 2014. Served as President from January 2010 to September 2025.
people.quote: Brian T. Moynihan (66) Chair of the Board since October 2014, and Chief Executive Officer, and member of the Board of Directors since January 2010.

people.name: Thong M. Nguyen
people.title: Vice Chair, Head of Global Strategy & Enterprise Platforms
people.bio: Previously served as Vice Chairman from January 2019 to October 2021 and Co-Head -- Consumer Banking from September 2014 to January 2019.
people.quote: Thong M. Nguyen (67) Vice Chair, Head of Global Strategy & Enterprise Platforms since October 2021;

people.name: Thomas M. Scrivener
people.title: Chief Operations Executive
people.bio: Previously served as Head of Consumer, Small Business & Wealth Management Operations from October 2019 to October 2021 and Global Real Estate and Enterprise Initiatives Executive from September 2018 to October 2019.
people.quote: Thomas M. Scrivener (54) Chief Operations Executive since October 2021;

people.name: Bruce R. Thompson
people.title: Vice Chair, Head of Enterprise Credit
people.bio: Previously served as Vice Chairman, President of the EU & Switzerland and CEO of Bank of America Europe DAC from May 2018 to December 2020. Served as Chief Financial Officer from July 2011 to July 2015.

people.name: Matthew M. Koder
people.bio: Listed as a non-CEO named executive officer for 2021 and for each year from 2023 through 2025. His current title and individual compensation total are not stated in the supplied text.
people.quote: 2025 & 2024 & 2023: Alastair M. Borthwick; Dean C. Athanasia; James P. DeMare; and Matthew M. Koder

people.name: Arnold W. Donald
people.title: Director
people.bio: Donald served as President, Chief Executive Officer, and Chief Climate Officer of Carnival from July 2013 to November 2022. He previously led The Executive Leadership Council and the Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation International and held senior leadership positions at Monsanto.
people.quote: Mr. Donald has more than three decades of strategic planning, global operations, and risk management experience in regulated, consumer, retail, and distribution businesses.

people.name: Monica C. Lozano
people.title: Director
people.bio: Lozano served as Chief Executive Officer of College Futures Foundation from December 2017 to July 2022 and previously served as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of ImpreMedia. She also serves on the boards of Apple and Target.
people.quote: Ms. Lozano brings a broad range of leadership experience in the public and private sectors

people.name: Maria N. Martinez
people.title: Director
people.bio: Martinez served as Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer of Cisco Systems from 2021 to 2024. She previously held senior executive roles at Salesforce and managed Microsoft's Global Services business.
people.quote: Ms. Martinez is a seasoned technology executive who brings extensive technology, risk management, customer experience, and strategic planning experience for complex, global businesses to our Board.

people.name: Brian T. Moynihan
people.title: Chair of the Board
people.bio: Moynihan has served as Chief Executive Officer since January 2010 and Board Chair since October 2014, and served as President from January 2010 to September 2025. He attends meetings of all Board committees.
people.quote: Mr. Moynihan, our Chair and CEO, leads our company in the execution of our strategic vision and our focus on Responsible Growth.

people.name: Lionel L. Nowell III
people.title: Lead Independent Director
people.bio: Nowell served as Senior Vice President and Treasurer of Pepsi from 2001 to May 2009 and previously served as Chief Financial Officer of The Pepsi Bottling Group. As Lead Independent Director, he attends meetings of all Board committees.
people.quote: Mr. Nowell, our Lead Independent Director, exemplifies strong independent Board leadership.
